subject: SIG: Dedicated GPU affinity and eviction workflow clarifications

Subject: SIG follow-up: GPU tenancy / noisy neighbour concerns

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our security team had a couple of follow-ups specific to Dedicated capacity: they want a short write-up clarifying runtime affinity (how customer workloads are pinned to GPUs), eviction behavior under GC/eviction pressure, and evidence that KV-cache and model weights are not accessible across tenants.

Specifically:
- Do you support NUMA/affinity pins at the process or container level?
- What triggers an eviction and what is the typical observable window for a running inference request?
- Any logs/artifacts that show KV cache isolation and eviction traces we can include in our SIG response?

Could you send this to me by EOD Thursday (1/14)? If helpful we can carve a short Zoom for a live walkthrough.

Best,
Julia

Acme Corp

Attached the sanitized eviction trace and a short note on what you should highlight to the customer:
- Eviction is a controlled preemption triggered by scheduler when node-level memory or GPU compute pressure crosses configured SLO thresholds.
- Active in-flight requests are allowed to finish up to a configurable grace-period; long requests beyond the grace period are failed with a well-defined error code (INFERENCE_EVICTED).
- We record eviction events in the node-events log and surface them in the Console trace with the request id for audit.

Files attached: eviction-runbook.md (runbook + thresholds) and kvcache-isolation-logs.tar.gz (metadata-only logs showing per-tenant cache hits).

Diego
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Julia Shepard <j.shepard@acme.com>, Acme Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 10:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: GPU tenancy / noisy neighbour concerns

Hi Julia — attaching the artifacts Diego and Priyom prepared. Short answers inline below and attachments linked for the SIG doc:

Quick answers:
- Affinity/pinning: We use container runtime GPU device assignment + cgroup CPU affinity. Processes are bound to GPU devices at container start; we do not perform live migration of GPU device bindings between tenants.
- Eviction behavior: Eviction is scheduler-driven at node level based on memory/compute thresholds. In-flight requests enter a grace window (configurable, default 6s) after which they fail with INFERENCE_EVICTED. We log request id and reason.
- KV-cache isolation: KV-cache entries are stored in per-tenant namespaces in memory and guarded by process ownership; logs show no cross-tenant cache hits.

Attachments: gfx-node-diagram.pdf, eviction-runbook.md, kvcache-isolation-logs.tar.gz

If you want a short live walkthrough, I'm available Thu 1/14 at 3pm PT — I'll bring Diego and Priyom.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: gfx-node-diagram.pdf]
